design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (road_hazard_claims), revised in round 2. Draw: prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[5,6,6]; counter posting 5, out-of-area replacement 6, Life-of-Tread cancellation 6.
WHY A GOOD TEST: the holder only asks to cancel her Life-of-Tread certificate because her 4Runner went onto her business fleet roster on 2026-10-01. The refund deducts benefits paid, and the refund rule waits on two states: every technician-recorded damage carries its replacement entry, and every claimable out-of-area replacement carries its reimbursement entry. The records show the 2026-08-22 RR damage reading without a replacement entry and a 2026-09-27 outside-merchant charge (326.50); asked, the holder tells of the store replacement and of her son's Wyoming replacement. The agent must post and reimburse first, then compute the refund from four other categories' records (tires, card, fleet, alignment) and the claim history.
SCOPE: task 0 owns hazard_ext_lot_cancellation_refund (confirm_life_of_tread_cancellation_58ab2fcf, user), hazard_ext_counter_replacement_posting (post_hazard_counter_replacement_324c4972), hazard_ext_outside_replacement_reimbursement (reimburse_hazard_outside_replacement_5f5d3272); task 1 owns the other three. Disjoint, jointly complete.
PROBLEM-TREE CARD: E1 root -> counter posting: value_input on benefits_paid, state form 'The Life-of-Tread cancellation refund is fixed only after every tire that a Crestline technician's inspection recorded as damaged on the covered set during the term carries its replacement entry on the certificate.' (only the counter posting writes a replacement entry for an earlier day's damage reading; the store authorization is for same-day readings). E2 root -> out-of-area replacement: value_input on benefits_paid, state form (round 2, O1) 'The Life-of-Tread cancellation refund is not paid until every out-of-area tire replacement that the holder can still claim within the receipt window carries its out-of-area replacement reimbursement entry on the certificate.' (only the out-of-area replacement policy writes that entry). False at the opening: dmg reading RR wear_pattern damage with only the April RR repair on the certificate; card charge M-2609271183 2026-09-27 with no reimbursement entry. Order: the two prerequisites commute (swapped replay gives the same terminal hash), then the holder's confirmation. Deletion: skipping the posting gives 86.63, skipping the reimbursement 134.28 (gold 29.03).
BASE-INVARIANT CARD: both claims inherit certificate_active (active) and within_plan_term (effective 2024-11-09 + 72 calendar months = 2030-11-09 inclusive; 2026-08-22 and 2026-09-27 inside; 2030-11-10 would fail). Commercial use is judged on the service date (O8): both service dates precede the 2026-10-01 enrollment and usage_class is personal. Defect exclusion: the technician recorded damage. The out_of_area mixed gate is retired for the out-of-area replacement scope by a declared overwrite restating the condition (receipt location near Rawlins, WY). The cancellation inherits certificate_active_cancel; the policy covers only certificates bought in cash/debit or on a bank card (O6), this one bank_card; the pro_rata scope holds (bought 2024-11-09, claims on file).
BUSINESS-OBJECT CARD: certificate RH-21480377 on set T-21480377 (5 Highway Terrain LT incl. full-size spare, unit 249.99, instant savings 50.00). Posting object: RR, damage reading 4/32 on 2026-08-22 at store #2214, odometer 74500. Reimbursement object: LF at Rawlins Tire & Service, receipt tire 289.50 + mounting 32.00 + disposal 5.00 = 326.50, tread 5/32, photo only. Excluded: the April RR repair (only the position's repair count), the 2024 card late fee (outside the window), older rotation readings.
FACTOR CARD (tier / baseline figure): posting 57.60 — price rule: instant-savings net 239.99 (unit -> 60.00); card +5 (-> 45.60); tire-care +3 (-> 50.40); bundle +4 (-> 48.00); repair points -4, one covered RR repair (-> 67.20); points apply only to a prorated percentage (C1); all baselines 40.00. Out-of-area 105.25 — proration measure: miles (rotation 2026-07-11, 49600 miles -> 23%) vs months (66% -> 208.44); card cap uplift +50 (-> 93.25); own price 239.99 vs unit 249.99 (-> 108.25); care +3 (-> 98.05); bundle +4 (-> 95.65); service allowance 33.25 (-> 72.00); all baselines 132.00. Refund 29.03 — clock from enrollment 2026-10-01 (-> 25.59); 30-day periods 50/72 for 23 months in force (calendar months -> 25.59); tread-life x0.9, LF 5/32 share 0.25 (-> 48.12); fee 0 (-> 4.03); unused-call credit 40.00 (-> 0.00); bundle clawback 20.00 (-> 49.03); all baselines 0.00.
METHOD PAIRWISE TABLES: counter price rule — fleet net vs instant-savings net: ticket tender (fleet_account vs other); instant-savings vs unit: set_instant_savings>0 with tire_count>=min; fleet vs unit: tires invoice discount present. Out-of-area proration — miles vs lower-of: rotation age <=120 vs 121-365 days; lower-of vs months: rotation within 365 days; miles vs months: a recent rotation. Own price — as the counter price rule. LOT day count — actual days vs 30-day periods: months in force <12 vs 12-35; 30-day vs calendar months: 12-35 vs >=36; days vs months: <12 vs >=36. LOT clock — enrollment date vs request date: open roster enrollment; request vs cancellation date: a pending request; enrollment vs cancellation: open enrollment.
SEED LEGALITY SWEEP (round 2): tires — Highway Terrain LT fits suv_cuv, 5 tires = max_tires_per_ticket, spare in rotation, rotations about every 3 months; Life-of-Tread entry gate passenger/suv/minivan personal; alignment — Lifetime Alignment Plan on a personal SUV, sold on the tire ticket, purchase_price 209.99 = 249.99 - tire_bundle_discount 40.00 (fixed); card — Auto Care Mastercard limit 5000 within 1000-5000 (fixed), APR 29.99, late fee 30.00; fleet — Starter, per_invoice billing (fixed), credit 4000 <= 5000, one roster vehicle within 1-4, business profile.
PERSONA: brisk owner; volunteers only the cancellation and its reason; ZIP/DOB/email when asked; the August counter replacement and the Wyoming replacement only on the agent's questions; agrees; confirms; ends.
STANDARD SOLUTION: locate/verify -> certificates, claim history, cancellation requests, tire set, tire events, vehicle, fleet account, roster, card account, card ledger, alignment plan -> post RR (57.60, 24%, 239.99, tread 4, odometer 74500) -> reimburse LF (105.25, 30%, tread 5, bank_card) -> hand over the cancellation; refund 29.03 to bank_card.
PROBE TABLE: see worklog.md (round 2) — card/alignment/fleet reads filtered by status and account; tire reads by covered set; damage reading absent -> posting out of scope; rotation absent -> months basis; pending request absent -> cancellation date; no zero divisions.
VERIFICATION: per-task gates (round 2) EXTENDED/REPLAY/SOLVABILITY/COMPUTE/GROUNDING OK; factor independence checked mechanically (0 violations).
REVISIONS (round 2): C3(d) certificate-wide repair points removed from the out-of-area replacement; C1 points apply only to prorated percentages; O1 E2 state form; O6 tender scope; O8 service-date judgement; alignment price fixed; card limit and fleet billing fixed; world re-dated to keep the refund positive.
user_scenario: You are Philippa Achterberg-Moss, 57, who runs a small garden-design business out of Worthington, Ohio. You speak quickly and practically, like someone squeezing a call in between client visits, and you like to get to the point. You open by saying you're calling about the road hazard protection on your 2022 Toyota 4Runner: on October 1st you put the 4Runner on your company's Crestline fleet account because it's now the business truck, so you want to cancel the personal road hazard plan on it today and get whatever refund is due. You give your phone number, 6145550241, straight away. Only when the agent asks for another detail to confirm who you are do you give your billing ZIP code, 43085; if they ask for more, your date of birth is March 9, 1969 and your email is philippa@achterbergmossgarden.com. The business name on the profile is Achterberg-Moss Garden Design LLC. You want the agent to handle everything that has to be handled on their side, and you will confirm the cancellation yourself when they put it in front of you. You paid for the tires and the plan back in November 2024 with your regular bank credit card, and the refund should go back the same way. You don't know what the refund should come to and you have no figure in mind. You don't think of anything else as open on the plan. Only if the agent asks about a tire being looked at or replaced in late August do you remember that your husband Doran took the truck to the Worthington store on August 22nd: they found a gash in the sidewall of the right rear tire and put a new tire on that afternoon; Doran said the protection-plan part would be sorted out and he paid the difference at the counter in cash; you don't know any of the amounts. If the agent asks whether anyone bought a tire somewhere other than Crestline, or asks about a charge of $326.50 on your Crestline Mastercard from September 27th, you explain that your son Emmett had the 4Runner on a trip out west: on September 27th he hit a deep pothole on I-80 just outside Rawlins, Wyoming, which broke the left front tire, and Rawlins Tire & Service replaced it. The receipt shows the tire at $289.50, mounting and balancing $32.00 and old-tire disposal $5.00, $326.50 in all, with the damaged tire's tread written as 5/32, paid on your Crestline Mastercard; the shop wrote 'impact break' on it. Emmett kept the damaged tire's photos and the receipt, which you have in your email and can forward right now, but the old tire stayed in Wyoming. You know the nearest Crestline stores are hundreds of miles from Rawlins. You had assumed the plan only worked at Crestline stores, which is why you never mentioned it. If the agent explains that one or both of those need to go through the plan before the cancellation, you say that's fine and to go ahead. When the agent tells you the refund amount and hands you the cancellation to confirm, you confirm it as given. Once the agent says the cancellation is done and the refund is on its way to your card, you thank them and end the call. You never mention the fleet account's details beyond the date the truck went on it, and you don't ask about anything else.
